title: Alex Eala rallies past Talia Gibson, advances to quarter-finals in Tokyo

   Alex Eala rallies past Talia Gibson, advances to quarter-finals in Tokyo
 Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox
 The Philippines’ Alex Eala hits a return against Australia's Talia Gibson during the WTA Pan Pacific Open on Oct 28.
 PHOTO: AFP
 Published   Oct 28, 2026, 10:06 PM
 Updated   Oct 28, 2026, 11:38 PM
 Set as preferred source Listen TOKYO – Philippine sensation Alexandra Eala came from behind to beat Talia Gibson 4-6, 6-2, 6-0 in Tokyo on Oct 28, and said later that “it took a lot to turn that match around”.
 The world No. 19’s recent run of early tournament exits looked in danger of continuing when Australia’s Gibson, ranked 38, took the first set at the Pan Pacific Open.
 But Eala dug in and evened the match before hitting top gear in a dominant third set.
 The 21-year-old said the turnaround had been “a gradual increase of level”.
 “Maybe just a couple of small details that when accumulated make a big difference,” she said.
 “In one 30-all, I went more for my shot, or in one deuce, I did so and so,” added Eala. “Those little details when all summed up, that’s the difference.”
 Eala faces Russian third seed Diana Shnaider in the quarter-finals.
 She became the first player from the Philippines to win a title on the women’s WTA Tour in August, and her every move is big news at home.
 Eala was again backed by passionate support in Tokyo, but she was on the ropes in the first set as Gibson punished her for missing chances.
 She began her comeback in the second set, but still let her opponent off the hook on several occasions.
 Eala went from strength to strength as the match moved into the final set, and closed it out when Gibson dumped a shot into the net.
 She hit nine aces and broke Gibson’s serve six times in the match.
 “Of course the support helps a lot all the time,” said Eala.
 “It creates a great atmosphere, and I think there was a bit of back and forth within the crowd,” she said. “You want to be present. You’re very invested in the match, so it comes naturally to focus.”
 Shnaider beat Aliaksandra Sasnovich of Belarus 6-3, 6-7 (5/7), 6-3 to book her place in the quarter-finals.
 World No. 1 Elena Rybakina plays her opening match on Oct 29 when she takes on fellow Kazakh Yulia Putintseva.
 Home favourite Naomi Osaka is also in action against Slovakian wild card Mia Pohankova. AFP
